source.row_text: | Replay old verdict, identical successful request/key | 200 with original verdict record/receipt, created=false; no extra cap count. |

| Replay old verdict with fresh key/path | duplicate_path or duplicate_content audit attempt, no new verdict; if bytes/path are changed, duplicate_head blocks at round_open without an exact head_repeat grant. A fabricated new textual review is still possible with the host token, but costs a legitimately opened round and is only host-attested. |

expect.note: fresh key+path hits duplicate_path or duplicate_content; changed bytes/path hit duplicate_head at round_open without exact head_repeat grant

source.row_text: | Verdict for a job claimed on another host | host_mismatch attempt, no record. Exception only for a centrally minted cross-host tester claim with exact review_of and host, matching round/head/task; then a verdict records the submitting host and tester job id. |

expect.note: exception only via centrally minted cross-host tester claim

source.row_text: | Grant for a different job/claim/action/round/head | grant_invalid attempt. Grant remains unconsumed on its own job. A key copied from another job does not cross its namespace. |

expect.note: grant naming different job/claim/action/round/head stays unconsumed on its own job

source.row_text: | Two testers on one head (hk 1901) | Separate numbered rounds and distinct tester claims; second requires a one-use head_repeat grant naming the earlier round and second tester. At cap also requires extension. Both verdicts persist; neither is overwritten or voided. BLOCKER after PASS prevents join until a further authorized PASS resolves it. This is the decided Q2=a resolution of hk 1901; installed policy enables it, while a missing exact grant still gives duplicate_head. |

expect.note: separate numbered round + distinct tester claim; head_repeat naming earlier round+second tester; at cap also extension; both verdicts persist; BLOCKER after PASS prevents join

source.row_text: | Builder forges content_sha256 | Server hashes exact bytes and rejects mismatch with invalid_request attempt. If builder submits invented bytes and their correct hash, the stored verdict accurately attests those bytes and host credential, not truthful review. O3 does not establish same-host reviewer authorship. |

| Server loses a write after acknowledging | Normal protection: content/journal/grant consumption/receipt relay commit in one PostgreSQL durable transaction, synchronous_commit=on, no 2xx before Commit. Client/director retains generation/seq/hash receipt. If a client/director observes a lower seq, changed generation, or a different hash at a retained seq, it locally emits history_regressed and refuses further authority use. This is a client/consumer code, not a server response or wrk_attempt record. It requests the operator recovery freeze; the server then returns wrk_recovery_required. A regressed server cannot detect its own missing history without an external witness; no lower count is accepted by a witnessing consumer. Lost receipt with surviving write is recovered by successful-key replay. Total destruction of both server history and independent receipts cannot be detected by a journal alone and is outside the actor bound. No false claim of solving Byzantine storage. |

request.note: consumer observes lower seq/changed generation/different hash at a retained seq

expect.note: client/consumer code, not a server response; requests operator recovery freeze

source.row_text: | Clock skew between hosts | Host time is asserted metadata only; server seq orders all operations. Grant expiry uses server UTC at consumption. Result is a normal record with server received_at; skew cannot buy more slots or resurrect a grant. A bad server clock is deployment failure; freeze grants until corrected rather than using host time. |

expect.note: server seq orders all ops; grant expiry uses server UTC at consumption; skew buys no slots

source.row_text: | Leaked desktop/mac-dev/mac-work/rpi token | Attacker/agent can submit host-attested evidence and consume valid grants for jobs already assigned to that id, and read fleet evidence. It can mint only the §2 scoped review assignment for its own active subject; it cannot mint root/builder/worker claims or grants, write another host's jobs without a central cross-host assignment, or exceed counters. Each accepted write records the leaked client id; denied operations create scope/host attempts. Operator rotates that host credential and pauses affected jobs. No proof of which pane leaked/used it. |

expect.note: attacker can submit host-attested evidence and consume grants for that host's jobs only; cannot mint root/builder/worker claims or grants

source.row_text: | Leaked director-1/operator-desk token, including shared-user mbp use | Valid privileged records can be minted within API checks. This breaks authority assumptions for the whole fleet, not just mbp jobs; revoke/rotate and audit central records. Per-host least privilege bounds builder-only host compromise, not privileged-token theft. |

expect.note: valid privileged records within API checks; revoke/rotate and audit central records

source.row_text: | Two simultaneous grant consumers, or extension followed by void then reuse | Job lock and unique consumption constraints choose one winner; second is sequence_conflict until refresh, then grant_consumed. A void record never returns grant capacity. |

expect.note: job lock + unique consumption pick one winner; second is sequence_conflict until refresh then grant_consumed; void never returns grant capacity

source.row_text: | Builder plants fake legacy events before import or erases real events | Only import records result; asserted authors remain untrusted. Activation reserves at least three used slots; no forged PASS, parent or grant is promoted. Incomplete history blocks evidentiary acceptance and produces migration warning; fresh review uses explicit extension. |

expect.note: only import records result; asserted authors untrusted; baseline>=3; no forged PASS promoted

source.row_text: | Builder deletes all local events or selects another inbox/hk binary | Existing canonical records remain unchanged. Director rejects fake/missing receipts and reads server. Local fake OK and hidden review effort are possible; no accepted server transition results. |

expect.note: director rejects fake/missing receipts; canonical records unchanged

source.row_text: | Server commits but reply/local projection is lost | Retried original key returns original record; GET repairs projections. No duplicated round/grant consumption. Local transport warning is not permission to proceed with a new tester. |

expect.note: retried original key returns original record; GET repairs projections; no duplicated consumption

source.row_text: | Legacy client posts job.joined directly, or task refs are relinked | Receipt fence rejects with wrk_receipt_required; no terminal relay/task mutation. Canonical claim remains unchanged. Unknown task/job completion cannot release quota at the director. |

expect.note: no terminal relay/task mutation; unknown completion cannot release quota

source.row_text: | End races open/verdict/grant | Serialized journal: if end wins, new mutation is job_ended; if mutation wins, its record precedes end. There is no ambiguous timestamp ordering. |

expect.note: serialized journal: if end wins mutation is job_ended; if mutation wins its record precedes end; no ambiguous timestamp ordering
